integrated_description: Upon a complaint, the manager first conducts an immediate safety and compliance triage to rule out any health or regulatory concerns before any other action. The manager then delivers a guest-experience-focused apology (without admitting fault), runs a rapid objective checklist—batch/recipe adherence, holding time and temperature, ticket specs, substitutions, and plating—before deciding to remake or comp; if a remake is warranted, it is coordinated privately with the chef as 'returning the plate to our stated standard' rather than a public override, and any replacement is explicitly framed as restoring compliance with the restaurant's official standard rather than accommodating personal preference. A structured post-incident review follows, producing a documented close-the-loop communication to the guest and triggering SOP corrections only when execution drift is confirmed—never when the issue is an expectation mismatch—treating culinary authenticity as non-negotiable throughout.
integration_rationale: All three modifications share a common backbone—protect authenticity, sequence actions objectively, and document outcomes—allowing them to be layered into a single escalating protocol: safety triage first (stakeholder_b), then no-fault apology plus objective checklist before any remake decision (stakeholder_a and stakeholder_c), private chef coordination framed as spec-restoration (stakeholder_c), and a post-incident review with guest close-the-loop and SOP adjustment only for confirmed execution drift (all three). No modification required abandoning another, so full coverage was achievable without compromise.
